gem-b1-first-professional-result.q: A small business owner types 'write a follow-up email' into Gemini and gets a generic, unusable message. What does the lesson say is the fix?
options: Ask Gemini to write three versions and pick one
Structure the prompt with role, context, specific requirements, format, and things to avoid
Switch to Gemini Live instead of typing
Repeat the request with more exclamation points
gem-b1-first-professional-result.why: Each part of the structured prompt removes a guess Gemini would otherwise have to make, replacing generic output with a usable draft.

gem-b1-first-professional-result.q: Why does the lesson say Gemini's prompt structure matters even more than for a standalone chatbot?
options: Gemini has stricter content filters than other tools
Gemini requires a paid plan to follow instructions
Gemini sits inside Gmail, Docs, and Sheets, where you need a usable result fast, not a back-and-forth chat
Gemini cannot remember context within one chat
gem-b1-first-professional-result.why: Because Gemini is embedded in Workspace apps, a structured first prompt matters more since there's less room for a slow back-and-forth.

gem-b1-first-professional-result.q: You've built a prompt template that reliably produces great follow-up emails. What's the recommended way to reuse it going forward?
options: Retype it from memory each time to keep it fresh
Paste the full example output as a new prompt every time
Only use it in Gemini Live
Turn it into a Gem with the role and requirements baked in as standing instructions
gem-b1-first-professional-result.why: The proTip recommends turning a proven prompt into a Gem so only the task-specific details need to be added each time.

gem-b2-prompting-fundamentals-multimodal.q: You attach a blurry photo of a delivery note and ask Gemini 'what is this?' What mistake does this match from the lesson?
options: Attaching a file but writing a vague prompt instead of stating the specific task
Cramming two unrelated tasks into one Task line
Skipping the Format part of the prompt
Using a file type Gemini doesn't support
gem-b2-prompting-fundamentals-multimodal.why: The lesson names this exact mistake: attaching a file but asking a vague question instead of stating what to do with it.

gem-b2-prompting-fundamentals-multimodal.q: What does the lesson say is the most common mistake once a file is attached to a Gemini prompt?
options: Forgetting to name a role
Not telling Gemini explicitly what to do with the file — describe it, extract from it, compare it — instead of assuming it will guess
Attaching more than one file at once
Using Gemini Live instead of the chat window
gem-b2-prompting-fundamentals-multimodal.why: Gemini will describe an attached image in general terms unless told exactly what to look for, extract, or compare.

gem-b2-prompting-fundamentals-multimodal.q: Per the lesson, what's true of Gemini's biggest practical edge over a text-only assistant?
options: It only works with typed text, never files
It requires a separate app for images and audio
It reads images, audio, video, and PDFs natively in the same chat as your text prompt
It can only process one file type per conversation
gem-b2-prompting-fundamentals-multimodal.why: The lesson states Gemini's biggest edge is reading images, audio, video, and PDFs natively alongside your text prompt in the same chat.

gem-b3-gmail-docs-daily-communication.q: You ask Gemini's Gmail side panel to draft a reply promising a specific delivery date you're not actually sure you can hit. What guardrail did you skip?
options: Asking Gemini to summarize the thread first
Reviewing the draft before sending
Using Help me write in Docs instead
Stating in the prompt what NOT to commit to, since Gemini doesn't know your real constraints unless told
gem-b3-gmail-docs-daily-communication.why: The 'do not commit to' line is the key guardrail because Gemini doesn't know your real pricing, dates, or approval limits unless told explicitly.

gem-b3-gmail-docs-daily-communication.q: In Google Docs, only one paragraph of a long draft needs a tone fix. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Select that paragraph and ask Gemini to refine just that section, rather than regenerating the whole document
Regenerate the entire document from scratch
Delete the paragraph and write it manually
Ask Gemini to summarize the whole doc first
gem-b3-gmail-docs-daily-communication.why: The lesson explicitly recommends refining just the section that needs it instead of regenerating the whole document.

gem-b3-gmail-docs-daily-communication.q: Why does the lesson warn against sending a Gemini-drafted email reply without reading the actual thread first?
options: Gemini cannot see the thread at all
You're accountable for what goes out, even though Gemini can see the thread it drafted from
Gemini drafts are always too short
The side panel doesn't save drafts
gem-b3-gmail-docs-daily-communication.why: The lesson stresses that you remain accountable for what's sent, so a draft needs review even though Gemini already saw the thread.

gem-i1-analyzing-documents-and-images.q: An insurance policy PDF and photos of water damage seem to disagree about the cause of damage. What should the prompt explicitly require Gemini to do?
options: Silently pick whichever source seems more reliable
Ignore the photos and trust the PDF only
Flag the disagreement clearly instead of resolving it silently
Ask a human to resolve it before responding at all
gem-i1-analyzing-documents-and-images.why: The value in cross-checking is Gemini surfacing a document-vs-image conflict explicitly rather than quietly resolving it in one direction.

gem-i1-analyzing-documents-and-images.q: Why does the lesson require the instruction 'answer only from the attached document and image(s)'?
options: It's a technical requirement for multi-file uploads
It reduces the file size Gemini needs to process
It's needed only for audio files, not documents
Without it, Gemini may blend general knowledge about contracts or listings with what's actually in your files, indistinguishably
gem-i1-analyzing-documents-and-images.why: This is the anti-hallucination guardrail: without it, Gemini blends outside knowledge with actual file content in a way you can't detect.

gem-i1-analyzing-documents-and-images.q: You upload a poorly lit, blurry photo alongside a document and expect precise detail extraction. What does the lesson say about this?
options: Quality in, quality out applies to files too — a blurry photo won't give reliable detail extraction
Gemini automatically enhances blurry images before analysis
This is fine as long as the document is high quality
Blurry photos are rejected automatically by Gemini
gem-i1-analyzing-documents-and-images.why: The lesson lists uploading a blurry or poorly lit photo and expecting precise extraction as a common mistake.

gem-i2-deep-research-grounded-reports.q: You enable Workspace sources for a Deep Research report combining your team's Gmail/Drive content with the public web. What should the brief explicitly request?
options: Nothing extra — Workspace sources are handled automatically
That internal findings be clearly separated from public-web findings, since they have very different reliability profiles
That only Drive content be used, excluding Gmail entirely
That the report skip citations for internal sources
gem-i2-deep-research-grounded-reports.why: The lesson stresses separating internal (primary-source) findings from public-web findings so their different reliability isn't blended together.

gem-i2-deep-research-grounded-reports.q: Before letting a Deep Research session run, the lesson says you should do what?
options: Immediately close the tab and check back in 30 minutes
Skip straight to reading the final report
Review the research plan Gemini proposes and adjust scope if it's missing an angle you care about
Disable Workspace sources for every run to save time
gem-i2-deep-research-grounded-reports.why: Skipping the plan review step is a named common mistake; reviewing it lets you correct scope before the run wastes time.

gem-i2-deep-research-grounded-reports.q: A one-line research question like 'tell me about competitor pricing' is submitted straight to Deep Research. What's the likely problem, per the lesson?
options: A vague request with no audience or scope produces a report covering the wrong angles
Deep Research will refuse to run
It will only search Gmail, not the web
It uses fewer citations than a scoped request
gem-i2-deep-research-grounded-reports.why: A vague one-line question with no audience or scope is listed as a common mistake that produces a report on the wrong angles.

gem-i3-sheets-data-workflows.q: You ask Gemini's Sheets side panel to 'flag rows with a big change' without a number. What happens, per the lesson?
options: Gemini asks a clarifying question before doing anything
Gemini defaults to a 10% threshold automatically
The formula fails to insert
'Significant change' gets interpreted arbitrarily since no numeric threshold was specified
gem-i3-sheets-data-workflows.why: Not specifying a numeric threshold is a named common mistake — the flagging condition ends up interpreted arbitrarily.

gem-i3-sheets-data-workflows.q: Why does the lesson say to name the exact column headers instead of saying 'the growth column'?
options: Column headers must be typed in all caps for Gemini to read them
Vague column references can lead Gemini to guess the wrong column
It's required to unlock the Sheets side panel
It speeds up formula calculation time
gem-i3-sheets-data-workflows.why: Vague column references force Gemini to guess, which is exactly the failure mode the lesson calls out.

gem-i3-sheets-data-workflows.q: After Gemini inserts a formula into your sheet, what should you do before trusting it?
options: Immediately copy it to every other tab
Ask for a full sheet rebuild to double-check
Spot-check it against 2-3 rows by hand, and ask for a plain-language explanation if you don't recognize the function
Nothing — inserted formulas are already verified by Gemini
gem-i3-sheets-data-workflows.why: The lesson requires reviewing and hand-checking the formula before accepting, and asking for a plain-language explanation to be able to maintain it.

gem-a1-notebooklm-vs-gemini.q: A law firm associate needs to know whether clause 4.2 in one specific vendor contract conflicts with the firm's standard terms, with zero tolerance for outside-knowledge blending. Which tool fits, per the lesson's decision framework?
options: NotebookLM, loading both documents as sources for a citation-backed answer
Gemini, using open web search
Gemini Deep Research without Workspace sources
Either tool works identically for this task
gem-a1-notebooklm-vs-gemini.why: A fixed, specific document set requiring zero outside-knowledge blending is exactly the scenario the lesson routes to NotebookLM.

gem-a1-notebooklm-vs-gemini.q: NotebookLM responds 'this isn't in your sources' to a question that actually needed outside context. What does the lesson say this response represents?
options: A bug that should be reported
The intended safety feature working as designed, not a limitation to route around
A sign to switch to a different NotebookLM notebook
Evidence the sources were uploaded incorrectly
gem-a1-notebooklm-vs-gemini.why: The lesson explicitly frames this refusal as NotebookLM's intended design, not a flaw — the tell-tale sign you picked the wrong tool for that question.

gem-a1-notebooklm-vs-gemini.q: A consultant needs a briefing combining a client's internal 40-page strategy doc with current public market data, with both types of source clearly separated. What's the recommended approach?
options: Use NotebookLM alone, since it handles both internal and public sources
Use Gemini alone with no source grounding
Use Gemini Deep Research with Workspace sources enabled, so it can read the Drive doc and the live web in one report
Manually copy both documents into a single chat message
gem-a1-notebooklm-vs-gemini.why: Scenario C in the lesson uses exactly this approach: Deep Research with Workspace sources to combine internal Drive content with live web research.

gem-a2-google-ecosystem-workflow.q: A team runs great Deep Research every month but the findings never get logged anywhere searchable, so decisions get forgotten. What failure mode does this illustrate?
options: Building a workflow too elaborate to run
Treating each tool as a separate silo instead of chaining research into a doc, tracker, and archive
Skipping the human review step
Forgetting to add source files to NotebookLM
gem-a2-google-ecosystem-workflow.why: The lesson's top listed mistake is treating each tool as a silo — great research that's never logged anywhere trackable.

gem-a2-google-ecosystem-workflow.q: Why does the lesson recommend a human review pass between the Deep Research export and the tracking Sheet or client-facing doc?
options: Deep Research reports cannot be exported directly to Docs
Human review is only needed for Workspace-sourced reports
An unreviewed report shouldn't go straight to a tracker or client without cutting off-target content and adding judgment calls
It satisfies a compliance requirement unrelated to accuracy
gem-a2-google-ecosystem-workflow.why: Skipping the human review step and letting an unreviewed report flow straight to a tracker or client is a named common mistake.

gem-a2-google-ecosystem-workflow.q: A colleague covering for a consultant asks a NotebookLM archive about a client decision made months earlier, in a cycle they weren't part of, and gets an accurate cited answer. What made this possible?
options: NotebookLM automatically syncs with every Gemini chat ever run
The consultant re-explained everything to the colleague beforehand
Gemini's memory feature retained the decision
The finished doc and source files were added to a standing NotebookLM notebook as part of the workflow
gem-a2-google-ecosystem-workflow.why: The workflow's archive step — adding the doc and source files to a standing NotebookLM notebook — is what made the decision findable later by anyone.
